newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan paper says Egypt tortures, deports students.
newsitem.headline: Sudan paper says Egypt tortures, deports students.

text.p: A Khartoum daily said on Sunday Egypt had tortured and deported four southern Sudanese students and detained 24 others because they belonged to rebel groups which have made peace with Sudan's Islamist government.

The privately-owned Akhbar al-Youm quoted Reverend Idi Ambrose, deputy president of parliament's human rights committee, as saying Egyptian authorities denied the students food and water and exposed them to a variety of tortures.
In Cairo, an Egyptian security official denied all Ambrose's charges, saying the goverment had offered all the help it could to Sudanese students.
"The ruling regime in Sudan is used to publishing lies intended to damage Egypt," the official was quoted in the Egyptian government-owned newspaper Al-Ahram as saying.

"We deny the accusations of Reverend Ambrose and what was published in Akhbar al-Youm. We have not arrested these students, we have given them all they want. Egypt is not punishing the Sudanese people for the actions of their government."

Ambrose was quoted as saying the students were members of two factions which broke away from the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), which has fought for more than a decade for autonomy of the mainly Christian and animist south.
The two factions signed peace deals in April with the Khartoum goverment and the daily said the Egyptian authorities had tortured the students to make them recant their "peace-oriented" beliefs.
Relations between Egypt and Sudan have been strained since gunmen tried to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Ethiopia last year.

Egypt, which accuses Sudan of harbouring and training the Moslem militants trying to topple the Cairo government, says three of the gunmen are hiding in Sudan but Khartoum says they are not within its borders.
